Fresno website design has a particular reader to please. A lot of the people searching here are buying for a farm: a grower who needs a custom harvest crew, a shipper looking for a refrigerated hauler, a ranch manager whose tractor broke down in the middle of the season. They want to know what you do, where you go and how to reach you, and they want to know it from a phone in a truck cab. Everybody else in town, from the taqueria to the dentist, is selling to the families whose paychecks come out of that same economy.

Dominion Web Design Pro is Maurice Johnson. He writes every page by hand, shows you a free demo before you spend anything, and charges once: $497, $997 or $1,997.

The biggest farm county in the country, by the numbers

Fresno County's 2024 crop and livestock report put the county's gross agricultural production at $9,029,122,000, a record, and that total made it the top farm county in the United States again after Kern County held the title for 2023. Almonds led at about $1.46 billion, grapes came second at about $1.04 billion and pistachios third at about $860 million. The Board of Supervisors accepted the report on November 4, 2025.

Those are farm-gate values, not profits, but they explain the business directory. Behind every orchard sit the people who prune it, spray it, harvest it, cool the fruit, pack it, haul it, insure it, fix the equipment and keep the books. Most of those firms are small, and many of them are still found mainly by word of mouth, which works right up until a new grower moves in or an old customer retires.

Who is reading an ag business site, and what they need to see

The buyer changes from one kind of farm business to the next, so the first screen has to change too.

Kind of businessWho is searchingWhat has to be on the page
Custom harvest, pruning or spray crewsGrowers and ranch managersCrops you work, acreage you can handle, the counties you cover, how far ahead to book, and any license numbers you hold
Equipment sales and repairFarmers with a machine downBrands you service, whether you send a mechanic to the field, parts you keep on the shelf and a phone number that works with one tap
Hauling and cold freightPackers, shippers and brokersTrailer types, lanes you run, your authority and insurance details, and a short quote form
Packing, cooling and storageGrowers choosing where to send fruitCommodities you handle, capacity, food safety programs you take part in and who to call during harvest
Ag bookkeeping, insurance and consultingFarm families and managersPlain descriptions of each service, who does the work and an easy way to book a first conversation

None of these buyers wants to read a slogan. They want a fact that tells them you can handle their job. Maurice asks what those facts are before he writes a line.

Fresno web design for a city of many languages

Census QuickFacts counts Fresno at 542,107 people in the 2020 Census, with 50.6% Hispanic or Latino and 14.2% Asian in its 2019 to 2023 estimates. The Pew Research Center's analysis of 2017 to 2019 survey data put the Fresno metro's Hmong population at about 35,000, the second largest of any metro area after Minneapolis and St. Paul. A University of California Cooperative Extension advisor has reported more than 900 Hmong farmers among over 1,300 Southeast Asian farms in Fresno County, based on a 2007 survey, many of them growing Asian specialty crops for farmers markets and restaurants.

Punjabi Sikh families are part of the same story. Sikh immigrants began building trucking businesses in the 1980s, and reporting on that community describes a Fresno-based group that advises drivers and publishes a magazine called Punjabi Trucking. A hauler, a corner market and a farm labor contractor in Fresno may each have customers who read a different language first.

Here is the honest part: Maurice writes in English. He will not run your pages through a translation tool and call them finished. If you need Spanish, Hmong or Punjabi pages, plan on a fluent speaker writing or checking that text, and raise it when you ask for your demo.

Places Fresno customers type into the search bar

Google says local results depend on relevance, distance and prominence. Distance is fixed, but a site can make it plain where you are and how far you travel, and the names people actually use help with that.

Tower District

Centered on Olive and Wishon avenues and named for the Tower Theatre, it is the city's arts and nightlife pocket, with coffee shops, vintage stores and breweries in older storefronts.

Fulton Street downtown

The six-block Fulton Mall reopened to cars in October 2017, for the first time in more than 50 years, with two-way traffic, parking and wide sidewalks. Downtown owners there have spent years filling empty storefronts.

Fig Garden Village and River Park

Fig Garden Village sits at Palm and Shaw avenues near Old Fig Garden; River Park is the north Fresno shopping village near Highway 41. Salons, clinics and boutiques here draw from the northern neighborhoods.

Clovis next door

Clovis is its own city on Fresno's northeast side, and its residents often search by that name. If you serve both, each deserves an honest section rather than one line that says "Fresno area."

One example owner, walked through

Picture a two-truck mobile repair business that fixes tractors, sprayers and forklifts on farms south and west of town. Today its customers call the owner's cell, and new ones find him only when a neighbor passes the number along. Here is how Maurice would build that site.

  • A home page that leads with the field call. "We come to you" in the first line, the counties covered, the machine brands handled and a tap-to-call button.
  • A service page for each kind of machine. Tractors, sprayers, forklifts and packing line equipment each get a short page, because that is how people search.
  • A plain harvest-season note. Expected response times when every grower needs help the same week, so nobody is surprised.
  • Photos from his own phone. His trucks, his shop and real jobs, never stock pictures of somebody else's equipment.

That owner would likely start with Starter at $497: five hand-written pages, a contact form that emails every lead, map and hours, titles and a sitemap submitted to Google, live in 7 to 14 days. If he works a dozen small towns, Pro at $997 adds ten researched city pages, Google Business Profile setup and an AI chat widget that is free for 14 days and then $297 a month. Agency at $1,997 researches the whole service area first and builds a page for each worthwhile town and service, usually 30 to 60, in waves with the first live inside two weeks; its AI phone agent setup is included, and the agent itself is free for 7 days, then $297 a month for up to 750 minutes. Hosting, maintenance and updates are $49 a month, or included while you keep an AI agent. We do not sell page counts: a page gets written because a search needs it.

No-cost help for Fresno owners

  • Valley Community SBDCHosted by Clovis Community College since 2018 and part of the UC Merced regional SBDC network, it gives free, confidential advising to owners and would-be owners in Fresno, Madera, Kings and Tulare counties.
  • Fresno Chamber of CommerceIts economic development resources page points owners to SCORE's free mentoring, the CalGold permit finder, the SBA and the Downtown Business Hub, which serves entrepreneurs in Spanish and English.
  • City of Fresno Economic DevelopmentOffers a "First-Stop for Startups" service, help with business tax, permits and code questions, and referrals to small business loans.

Built in East Texas for a Fresno business

Straight answer on location: Dominion Web Design Pro has no office in Fresno. Maurice Johnson builds every site from Big Sandy in East Texas and delivers it remotely, by link, phone and email.

During harvest you may only have time for a phone call at six in the morning. That works: send photos and a few notes when you can, and review the pages from your phone.

Tell us your business name, what you do and which crops, towns or customers you serve, and Maurice will build a free demo around them.

Common questions

How do I pick a Fresno web designer for an ag or trucking business?

Ask three things. Will they learn who actually buys from you (a grower, a broker, a shipper, a homeowner) before they write? Will they show you something before you pay? And what is the full cost for the first year, monthly charges included? We answer the last two up front: a free demo comes first, and the build is $497, $997 or $1,997 paid once, with hosting, maintenance and updates at $49 a month unless you keep one of our AI agents.

What do Fresno web design services usually include?

It varies by designer, so get the list in writing. Our Starter package covers five hand-written pages (home, services, about, contact, service area), a contact form that emails every lead, Google Maps and hours, titles, descriptions and a sitemap submitted to Google, and it goes live in 7 to 14 days. Pro adds a 10-page site with a photo gallery, Google Business Profile setup, schema markup, ten researched city pages and your Google reviews on the site.

How much does website design cost in Fresno, CA?

Quotes run from cheap builder subscriptions to several thousand dollars for a custom agency project. Ours are printed: Starter $497, Pro $997, Agency $1,997, each one time, and you own the finished site. Pro's AI chat widget is free for 14 days and then $297 a month if you keep it. Agency includes AI phone agent setup; the agent is free for 7 days, then $297 a month for up to 750 minutes, cancel any time.

Can you write my site in Spanish, Hmong or Punjabi?

No. Maurice writes in English and does not offer translation. If your customers or crews read another language first, the best route is copy written or checked by a fluent speaker you trust. Mention it when you ask for the demo so the plan accounts for it.

Is Dominion Web Design Pro located in Fresno?

No. Maurice Johnson builds every site remotely from Big Sandy in East Texas, and there is no Fresno office. Call (903) 636-7511 any hour; an AI receptionist answers and can transfer you to Maurice.
